title: Deterministic authored parametric surfaces and captured point attributes

supportedProfile: Bundle 0.3 surface program version 1, three typed scalar coordinate expressions over a fixed rectangular u/v domain
Fixed grid topology with explicit open/weld/duplicate seams and declared collapsed boundary poles
Analytic derivative or finite-difference normals, immutable float64 indexed triangle meshes and separate UV/base-position captures
Absolute-time and bounded scene-parameter evaluation consumed by the shared WebGL2/native TeX player
excluded: Arbitrary Blender Geometry Nodes or attribute-domain conversion
Adaptive or changing topology, remeshing, general implicit surfaces and numerical PDE solvers
Guarantees of manifoldness, global injectivity, outward orientation or equivalence to Blender output
Lighting, transparent shaded materials and hidden-surface removal for wireframe presentation

inputs: Explicit operation/resource IDs, mesh units, finite increasing u/v domain intervals and bounded integer segment counts
Dimensionless u/v locals, time in seconds, and declared typed scene parameters; coordinate outputs are dimensionless numbers interpreted in operation.units
Three coordinate expressions and either three dU/dV expressions or the finite-difference policy
At most 16 surface operations and 65536 total grid cells; deterministic failures on invalid domains, seams, units, degeneracy or budgets
outputs: Generated resources occur only in sampled frame.resources; authored bundles/packages retain the declarative programs and ordinary assets
Stable topologyRevision and indices for fixed domain, resolution, seam and pole choices; changing time/parameters regenerates finite positions, normals and bounds
frame.surfaces retains parameter coordinates and initial base positions alongside generation reports
Executed TeX JSON and decoded coordinate expressions remain archived with exact generated-source spans
coordinates: Resource chart is object-local, right-handed XYZ in explicit unit/m/cm/mm units, independent of document bp
u/v are authored numeric domain coordinates; captures are not silently normalized to 0..1
orientation uv follows dU cross dV; vu reverses the selected orientation
Instance/ancestor transforms and camera projection follow mesh generation; source geometry is not overwritten
errorPolicy: Nonfinite coordinates, invalid normals and undeclared degenerate geometry fail with diagnostics
Weld/duplicate seams require endpoint agreement within declared tolerance; deliberate poles must collapse consistently
Pole normals use the documented incident-face policy; analytic and finite-difference normals remain distinct approximation contracts
Literal TeX capture rejects duplicate JSON keys, unsafe sidecar paths, resource collisions and oversized JSON before publishing a bundle

verification.command: python -m unittest tests.surface_port_spec_test tests.surface_capture_test tests.surface_player_test -v; npm test
claims: The registered native TeX fixture compiles into declarative sphere and torus resources without authored mesh buffers
Browser tests check sphere/torus equations and bounds independently at sampled times and after parameter changes
Repeated/reverse captures preserve exact pixels in the same pinned browser and frozen source; generated topology remains unchanged
The focused registry validates this PortSpec independently of the historical four-scene raster baseline
notEstablished: Blender execution, byte-for-byte mesh equivalence or its complete test corpus
Identical raster bytes across different browsers, GPUs or drivers
Correct topology/normals for every arbitrary mathematical expression or undetected between-sample singularity
An analytical certificate of manifoldness or a solver for wave/PDE evolution
